name: Lychee
tagline: A hosted link-in-bio page with themes, custom domain support and click analytics.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A link-in-bio page is a list of links, an avatar, and a click counter. An agent can produce that in one sitting, including a redirect endpoint that logs clicks to SQLite and a tiny password-protected stats view. What you are actually buying from a hosted tool is that you never touch it again: custom domain SSL, uptime, mobile editing from your phone, and a theme that already looks finished. If your bio link going down for an afternoon would cost you real money, pay someone. If it points at four things and you already deploy stuff, build it.
coreLoopDIY: Renders a single public link page from a config file and routes every outbound click through a redirect that records it, with a password-gated stats page.
requirements: a host that runs Node, or any static host plus a small serverless function
a domain you control, for the vanity URL
basic comfort editing a config file to change links
whatYouLose: Editing your links from your phone in ten seconds without a deploy
Custom domain plus automatic SSL handled for you
A theme gallery and preview that already looks designed
Analytics beyond raw click counts: referrers, geo, time series, device breakdown
Someone else's uptime guarantee on the one URL in your bio
moatNotes: The category has no network effect, which is why there are forty of these. The defensible part is polish and never breaking.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a bio link is infrastructure that a non-technical person needs to edit constantly and can never afford to have broken. Paying a few dollars a month converts a deploy step into a text field, and converts a domain and cert you have to remember into something handled. That is a real trade, just not a technical one.
notes: The build is easy; the discipline of not redeploying your whole site to swap a link is the part you are actually buying out of.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted link-in-bio page. Stack: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), Tailwind CSS, better-sqlite3. No other dependencies, no CMS, no auth provider.

Structure:
- links.config.ts exports a profile object: displayName, bio, avatarPath, themeColor, and an ordered array of links. Each link has id, label, url, optional subtitle, optional emoji or icon path, and an enabled boolean.
- / renders the page from that config: centered column, avatar, name, bio, then stacked full-width link buttons. Mobile-first, large tap targets, dark mode via prefers-color-scheme. It must look finished, not like a form.
- Every link button points at /go/[id], not the destination URL.
- /go/[id] is a route handler: look up the id in links.config.ts, insert a row into the clicks table (id, timestamp, referrer, user agent string), then 302 to the destination. If the id is unknown, 404. Never block the redirect on the write failing.
- SQLite file path from DATABASE_PATH in .env, default ./data/links.db. Create the table on first run.
- /stats is gated by a single shared password compared against ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env, set as an httpOnly cookie after a simple login form. No user accounts. Show total clicks per link, clicks in the last 7 and 30 days, and top referrers. Plain tables, no chart library.
- Open Graph and Twitter card meta tags generated from the profile config.

Out of scope: themes gallery, drag-and-drop editor, multiple pages, email capture, payments, embedded media players, telemetry of any kind.

Include a .env.example with ADMIN_PASSWORD and DATABASE_PATH, a .gitignore covering .env and data/, and a README with run, build, and deploy steps plus a note on putting the SQLite file on a persistent volume.
